hopf-fibration.png.title: Hopf Fibration
hopf-fibration.png.creator: Niles Johnson
hopf-fibration.png.changes: User-supplied 2048 x 1820 resized version; copied byte-for-byte without further modification.
hopf-fibration.png.attribution: Hopf Fibration — Niles Johnson, CC BY 4.0. User-supplied resized copy; no further changes.
hopf-fibration.png.caption: Each colored point on the small sphere corresponds to a circle fiber in the three-sphere. The large shape is a projection of those fibers into a three-dimensional ball.
hopf-fibration.png.scope: Illustrates the Hopf fibration S^3 → S^2 with circle fibers. No established equivalence to the logistic map or a physical brane model is asserted.

sphere-eversion-poster.jpg.title: Sphere eversion using Thurston's corrugations — frame at 15 seconds
sphere-eversion-poster.jpg.creator: Carsten Steger
sphere-eversion-poster.jpg.changes: Single frame extracted at 15 seconds and resized to 640 x 640 with ffmpeg; distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
sphere-eversion-poster.jpg.source_upload_verified: User-provided WebM exactly matches the Commons original SHA1 and byte size (14793045).
sphere-eversion-poster.jpg.attribution: Sphere eversion using Thurston's corrugations — © 2022 Carsten Steger, CC BY-SA 4.0. Poster frame extracted at 15 s and resized.
sphere-eversion-poster.jpg.caption: A sphere turns inside out through smooth immersed surfaces. Self-intersections are allowed; tears, creases and pinch points are not.
sphere-eversion-poster.jpg.scope: A topology example, not collapse to a point and not a proved connection to logistic dynamics.

integration.video_policy: Use a user-initiated video with controls, preload=none, the local poster, and a link to the Commons source. Do not autoplay. The original video is 14.8 MB and 109.266 s.
integration.pdf_policy: Use a static figure and caption in PDFs, with a link to the web animation. Do not describe a static PDF image as animated.
integration.relationship_policy: Use solid links only for defined, proved mathematical implications. Use dashed exploratory links for the Hopf/sphere-eversion/logistic relationship until a mapping, preserved quantity and theorem are stated.
